## Grafana Cloud (Remote)

Grafana's hosted MCP server connects AI assistants to Cloud dashboards, metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and incidents. It also exposes Assistant-native tools, so its tool set differs from the local open source server.

### Setup

You need a hosted Grafana Cloud stack where Assistant is available and its terms have been accepted. Your user needs the Assistant Cloud MCP User role or the `grafana-assistant-app.cloud-mcp:access` permission; Editor and higher roles receive this permission by default. Run `thv run grafana-remote --remote-auth` and authorize with your Grafana identity. The service supports Client ID Metadata Documents and dynamic client registration, so ToolHive needs no pre-created OAuth application or service-account token. Keep the default ToolHive callback port when using its published client metadata.

The optional header `X-Grafana-URL` selects a stack, for example `--remote-forward-headers X-Grafana-URL=https://<YOUR_STACK>.grafana.net`; otherwise the authorization flow asks for it. For read-only access, clear both Query access and Write access during consent, because raw SQL query access can modify data. Usage counts toward Grafana Assistant billing and active users. Self-hosted Grafana instances use the existing local server. See the [Cloud MCP guide](https://grafana.com/docs/grafana-cloud/ai-tools/mcp-servers/cloud-mcp/) for roles, stack-specific URLs, and manual client registration when required by another client.
